# Phase 1 foundation architecture (retained by Phase 2)

> This documents the original Phase 1 foundation. The extended Phase 2 coordinate, arena, buffering, boundary, and origin-shift contract lives in [`ARCHITECTURE_PHASE2.md`](ARCHITECTURE_PHASE2.md).

## Scene graph (generated by the Editor tool)

```text
CesiumGeoreference
└── GooglePhotorealistic3DTiles    (Cesium3DTileset, URL source, credits on, physics meshes on)
└── TestCharacter                  (CharacterController + CesiumGlobeAnchor)
    └── CapsuleVisual              (visual mesh only; no gameplay collider)
    └── CameraPivot
        └── Main Camera            (third-person follow camera)
PhaseOneWorldSystems               (GeospatialWorldManager + PhaseOneRuntimeHud)
Directional Light
```

The tileset remains disabled until an API key is supplied. This avoids a knowingly invalid placeholder request. Once configured, the URL points at Google's root tileset document and Cesium handles incremental child-tile streaming.

## Responsibilities

- `GeoPosition` / `LocalPosition`: geographic WGS84 and metre-based ENU coordinates are distinct types (the Phase 2 contract is documented separately).
- `GeospatialWorldManager`: owns Cesium origin setup, URL configuration, ground collision probing, spawn placement, the stable arena ENU frame, and geospatial queries.
- `PhaseOneTestCharacterController`: local-only WASD/sprint/jump and third-person mouse orbit; no networking, shooting, or health.
- `PhaseOneRuntimeHud`: lets the tester choose coordinates and supply a local API key; shows the live anchor coordinates and ground-load state.
- `PhaseOneSceneBuilder`: creates a clean URP asset and the Phase 1 scene when the Editor first imports the project; also exposes a manual menu item.

## Physics caveat

`Create Physics Meshes` is enabled to test the concept. The capsule is held until the Cesium tileset has a collider beneath the origin, then uses Unity's `CharacterController`. During initial loading the temporary spawn camera tilts down so the target surface is visible; normal follow-camera pitch is restored after ground contact. The Cesium collision surface can be regenerated as streamed tiles refine or are culled. This is a deliberately small, camera-based proof—not a promise of stable production physics. Cesium documents that tile collision is best suited to camera raycasts/simple collision and recommends persistent proxy colliders for complicated simulations. Do not build production combat hitboxes or authoritative movement on this changing visual mesh.

## Original Phase 1 exclusions (some are addressed by later phases)

- No Unity Multiplayer Services, NGO, Transport, Relay, host migration, or dedicated server.
- No arena radius/boundary, lobby, shared link, accounts, or backend.
- No weapon, projectile, hit detection, health, death, respawn, or anti-cheat.
- No map scraping, offline tile cache, or extraction of Google geometry/metadata.
- No mobile/web target tuning. These are later phases after the local world proof.
